item.content:encoded:
Applications for the 2027–2029 Erasmus Mundus Master’s Program in Public Policy (Mundus MAPP) are expected to open on 1 September 2026, offering students from around the world the opportunity to complete an interdisciplinary, international Master of Arts in Public Policy across leading European universities.

Mundus MAPP is a two-year, full-time, in-person Erasmus Mundus Joint Master programme designed to prepare future leaders for careers in public policy, government, international organizations, development institutions, civil society, academia, and the private sector.

The programme is delivered by a consortium of four European institutions:

  • Central European University Private University (CEU PU)
  • International Institute of Social Studies of Erasmus University Rotterdam (ISS)
  • Institut Barcelona d’Estudis Internacionals (IBEI)
  • University of York

Students choose one of four mobility tracks covering Global Public Policy, European Public Policy, Political Economy and Development, or Governance and Development.

For outstanding applicants, the programme offers the prestigious Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters (EMJM) Scholarship. The scholarship is calculated at €1,400 per month for 24 months, providing a maximum scholarship value of €33,600, together with a full tuition-fee waiver. The monthly contribution is intended to assist students with living, travel, visa, installation, and related costs.

The scholarship application is integrated into the main Mundus MAPP admission application; there is no separate scholarship application.

For the 2027–2029 intake, candidates who want to be considered for financial aid must submit their applications by:

1 December 2026 at 23:59 Central European Time (CET).

The programme is open to applicants from both within and outside the European Union, subject to academic, mobility, English-language, and other admissions requirements.

About the Mundus MAPP Erasmus Mundus Master’s Program

Mundus MAPP is the Erasmus Mundus Master’s Program in Public Policy, a joint postgraduate programme supported by the Erasmus+ action of the European Union.

Its overall purpose is to provide both scholarly education and practical preparation for people who may become future policy leaders in:

  • Government
  • International organizations
  • Public administration
  • International development
  • Nonprofit organizations
  • Civil society
  • Think tanks
  • Research institutions
  • Academia
  • Private-sector organizations working on policy and governance

The programme aims to give students a detailed and systematic understanding of how:

  • Political institutions operate
  • Public policies are developed
  • Political processes interact with policy
  • International and transnational governance functions
  • Economic and political forces influence policymaking
  • European governance interacts with national and global processes

Mundus MAPP combines theoretical policy studies with practical exposure to real-world policymaking.

What Makes Mundus MAPP Different?

One of the defining characteristics of Mundus MAPP is its international mobility structure.

Instead of completing the entire degree at a single university, students study in two different countries and at two consortium institutions according to their chosen mobility track.

The programme is built around the belief that effective policy professionals need both:

  • The ability to understand and situate complex policy problems
  • The ability to develop and assess practical policy solutions

Students therefore combine academic learning with practical experiences such as:

  • Internships
  • Study trips
  • Case studies
  • Research projects
  • Interaction with policymakers and practitioners
  • Cross-cultural academic collaboration

Approximately 60% of the curriculum is common across the programme, while around 40% consists of track-specific coursework.

This structure gives all Mundus MAPP students a common foundation in policy studies while still allowing significant specialization.

Four Mundus MAPP Mobility Tracks

Applicants may apply to only one of the four available mobility tracks.

Each track combines two consortium institutions and leads to a different specialization.

1. CEU PU–IBEI Track: Global Public Policy

The CEU PU–IBEI track specializes in:

Global Public Policy

This pathway is particularly relevant to students interested in public-policy challenges extending across national borders.

Potential areas of interest may include:

  • Global governance
  • International organizations
  • Transnational policymaking
  • Global political economy
  • International development
  • International institutions
  • Cross-border policy challenges

Students study through Central European University and IBEI.

2. CEU PU–York Track: European Public Policy

The CEU PU–University of York track focuses on:

European Public Policy

It is particularly relevant for students interested in:

  • European governance
  • European institutions
  • Policy coordination
  • Multi-level governance
  • Public administration
  • European political processes

Students combine study at CEU with the University of York.

3. ISS–IBEI Track: Political Economy and Development

The ISS–IBEI track specializes in:

Political Economy and Development

This pathway may be especially attractive to students interested in relationships between:

  • Economic systems
  • Development
  • Inequality
  • Institutions
  • International political economy
  • Public policy
  • Social transformation

Students study through ISS and IBEI.

4. ISS–York Track: Governance and Development

The ISS–York track specializes in:

Governance and Development

The track provides a strong route for applicants interested in:

  • Governance
  • International development
  • Public institutions
  • State capacity
  • Development policy
  • Political and institutional change

Students combine study at ISS with the University of York.

Compulsory International Mobility

Physical mobility is a mandatory component of Mundus MAPP.

Every enrolled student must complete:

Two study periods in two different countries

with each study period comprising at least:

30 ECTS credits

Importantly, both countries must be different from the student’s country of residence at the time of application or enrollment.

For example, someone applying to the ISS–IBEI track must normally be resident outside:

  • The Netherlands
  • Spain

at the relevant application/enrollment stage.

Applicants must provide evidence of residence before enrollment.

Possible evidence can include:

  • Municipal residence certificate
  • Rental contract
  • Utility bills

The compulsory mobility requirement cannot be replaced with virtual study.

Degree Awarded

Students who successfully complete Mundus MAPP receive a:

Master of Arts in Public Policy

The degree is jointly awarded by the two consortium institutions attended by the student.

Graduates also receive a diploma supplement.

The MA qualification is recognized by the appropriate bodies in:

  • Austria
  • Netherlands
  • Spain
  • United Kingdom

Students studying on CEU tracks also receive a programme that fulfills the requirements for CEU’s Master of Arts degree in Public Policy registered with the New York State Education Department in the United States.

This gives the programme both European and, for CEU tracks, additional U.S.-accredited degree recognition.

Who Can Apply?

Mundus MAPP is open to:

European and third-country nationals.

In other words, eligibility is not limited to EU citizens.

Applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, the Americas, the Middle East, Oceania, and other regions may apply if they meet the academic, mobility, and language requirements.

Academic Qualifications

Applicants must hold a Bachelor’s degree representing at least:

Three years of university-level study

from a recognized university or higher-education institution.

Candidates need to have achieved at least:

Upper Second Class / 2.1, where applicable

and:

GPA of at least 3.17 out of 4.0 or equivalent.

Applicants must provide their GPA on a 4.0 scale.

If their university transcript uses another grading system, candidates may use conversion tools such as:

  • Scholaro GPA Calculator
  • WES iGPA Calculator

to determine an approximate 4.0-scale GPA.

Preferred Academic Background

Applicants with degrees in:

Social sciences or equivalent disciplines

are normally given preference.

This could potentially include areas such as:

  • Political science
  • International relations
  • Public policy
  • Economics
  • Sociology
  • Development studies
  • Social sciences
  • Governance studies
  • Related fields

However, applicants should judge their eligibility based on the formal programme requirements rather than assuming every degree in a broadly related area will automatically qualify.

Natural Sciences and Engineering Applicants

The admissions requirements explicitly state that candidates holding only a Bachelor’s degree in:

  • Natural Sciences
  • Engineering

are not eligible to apply.

Prospective candidates from multidisciplinary backgrounds should therefore review the programme’s academic eligibility rules carefully.

Applicants Who Already Hold a Master’s Degree

Having a previous master’s degree does not automatically make an applicant ineligible for Mundus MAPP.

However, candidates who already hold a master’s degree must also have obtained at least:

  • Upper Second / 2.1 where applicable, and
  • GPA of at least 3.17/4.0 or equivalent

during the master’s programme.

There is also an important scholarship consideration:

Priority for Erasmus Mundus scholarships is given to candidates who have not previously had the opportunity to study in a master’s degree programme.

This does not mean existing master’s degree holders cannot apply for Mundus MAPP. It means they may be at a disadvantage in the competition for limited scholarships.

Special Requirement for IBEI Tracks

Applicants selecting either:

  • CEU–IBEI, or
  • ISS–IBEI

must meet the requirements associated with Spanish higher-education regulations.

Their undergraduate degree must have been obtained from a fully accredited higher-education institution and must qualify the applicant for admission to master’s-level studies in the country where the undergraduate diploma was issued.

Motivation for Public Policy

Applicants are expected to demonstrate:

High motivation and interest in European and international public policy.

This is assessed through the:

Statement of purpose

The motivation statement is therefore a central component of the admission process.

A strong statement should explain more than simply why the applicant wants a master’s degree.

It should demonstrate:

  • Why public policy matters to the applicant
  • Which policy challenges interest them
  • Why Mundus MAPP is the right programme
  • Why the selected mobility track fits their objectives
  • What professional or academic trajectory they hope to pursue
  • How their previous education or experience prepares them for the programme

Mundus MAPP and the Use of AI in Applications

The programme acknowledges that applicants increasingly use artificial intelligence tools when preparing written materials.

However, Mundus MAPP explicitly emphasizes that it values:

Authentic and personal motivation statements.

Applicants should therefore ensure that their statement genuinely reflects their:

  • Experiences
  • Motivations
  • Intellectual interests
  • Career objectives
  • Personal reasons for choosing the programme

A generic or heavily automated statement may fail to communicate the individual qualities that admissions reviewers are looking for.

English Language Requirements

Mundus MAPP is taught in English.

Applicants who do not qualify for a language-test exemption must submit an accepted English-language test score with the application.

Late submission of English scores is not permitted.

Accepted tests and minimum scores include:

TOEFL iBT

95 or above

The test must have been taken within two years of the application deadline.

IELTS Academic

7.0 or above

The test must have been taken within two years of the application deadline.

Cambridge C2 Proficiency

C2 or above

The test must have been taken within five years of the deadline.

Cambridge C1 Advanced

C1 or above

The test must have been taken within five years of the deadline.

Pearson PTE Academic

76 or above

The test must have been taken within two years.

Duolingo English Test

130 or above

The test must have been taken within two years.

English-Language Test Exemptions

Applicants who are citizens of certain countries may be exempt if they completed a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree taught exclusively in English.

The listed countries include:

  • Australia
  • Botswana
  • Canada
  • Gambia
  • Ghana
  • Ireland
  • Jamaica
  • Kenya
  • Liberia
  • Malawi
  • Namibia
  • New Zealand
  • Nigeria
  • Philippines
  • Rwanda, English-speaking region
  • South Africa
  • Tanzania
  • Trinidad and Tobago
  • Uganda
  • United Kingdom
  • United States
  • Zambia

Applicants must still satisfy the degree-language conditions specified by the programme.

English Waiver for Other Applicants

Citizens of other countries may request an English-language waiver if they completed a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree taught exclusively in English in:

  • Australia
  • Canada
  • New Zealand
  • United States
  • European Union
  • United Kingdom
  • Iceland
  • Liechtenstein
  • Norway
  • Switzerland

or at eligible satellite campuses of U.S. or UK universities.

Candidates must provide supporting documentation confirming that the language of instruction was English.

Additional Requirements for ISS Tracks

Candidates applying for:

  • ISS–IBEI
  • ISS–York

who will require a student visa for the Netherlands may face additional English-language requirements connected with Dutch immigration procedures.

Applicants should therefore review the programme’s current visa-related language guidance before applying.

Is Work Experience Required?

No.

Professional experience is not a formal eligibility requirement.

Applicants can therefore apply directly from undergraduate study if they otherwise meet the admissions criteria.

However, the programme states that:

Candidates with relevant work experience receive preference.

Relevant experience could potentially include work or internships in areas such as:

  • Public policy
  • Government
  • International organizations
  • NGOs
  • Development
  • Research
  • Advocacy
  • Public administration
  • Think tanks
  • Policy consulting

Spanish Language Requirement

Spanish proficiency is:

Not required

for any Mundus MAPP track.

However, students studying through IBEI may have opportunities to take selected elective courses taught in Spanish during their second year.

Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarship

One of the most attractive features of Mundus MAPP is the availability of Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships for outstanding candidates.

The scholarships are open to top-ranked applicants from:

  • EU countries
  • Non-EU countries

A limited number are available and are awarded based on academic merit.

Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Value

The EMJM scholarship is calculated using a monthly unit cost of:

€1,400 per month

for:

24 months

This gives a maximum total scholarship value of:

€33,600

Scholarship recipients also receive:

A full tuition-fee waiver.

The €1,400 monthly contribution is intended to help students meet expenses including:

  • Subsistence
  • Installation
  • Travel
  • Visa-related costs
  • Other living and participation expenses

However, applicants should understand that this is a monthly scholarship payment rather than a promise that every individual expense will be separately reimbursed.

Costs Not Separately Covered by the EMJM Scholarship

The financial-aid information identifies several costs that students must meet themselves rather than expecting additional dedicated reimbursement.

These include:

  • Study Visit during Year 1, estimated at approximately €600–€1,000
  • Winter School during Year 2, estimated at approximately €600–€1,000
  • Travel and visa costs between the student’s home country and consortium countries
  • Travel connected with moving to the Year 2 university

The monthly €1,400 contribution can help students manage overall living and mobility costs, but applicants should budget carefully for these specific expenses.

Health Insurance

The Mundus MAPP Consortium purchases health insurance meeting relevant EACEA minimum requirements for:

All enrolled students.

Coverage applies for the study period and also extends for a limited period before and after the programme.

Additional Support for Students With Individual Needs

Additional financial support may be available to scholarship recipients with individual needs, depending on the level of disability or support required.

Applicants who may require such support should review the applicable Erasmus Mundus and programme provisions carefully.

Previous Erasmus Mundus Scholarship Holders

Applicants who have already received an:

Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarship

are not eligible to receive another EMJM scholarship.

Additionally, an EMJM scholarship holder cannot simultaneously benefit from another EU-funded scholarship scheme to undertake the same or another Erasmus Mundus Joint Master during the relevant enrollment period.

Mundus MAPP Institutional Scholarships

The Erasmus Mundus scholarship is not the only financial-aid route.

The Mundus MAPP Consortium also offers:

One Institutional Scholarship per study track.

There are four tracks, meaning this support is distributed across the programme’s mobility pathways.

Institutional Scholarship recipients receive:

50% tuition-fee waiver at both the Year 1 and Year 2 institutions.

However:

The Institutional Scholarship does not include a stipend.

Applicants should therefore distinguish between the two awards.

EMJM Scholarship

  • €1,400 monthly contribution
  • Up to €33,600 over 24 months
  • Full tuition-fee waiver

Institutional Scholarship

  • 50% tuition waiver
  • No living stipend

No Separate Scholarship Application

Applicants do not complete a separate Erasmus Mundus scholarship application.

During the normal Mundus MAPP application, candidates indicate whether they wish to be considered for financial aid.

Applicants who submit by the scholarship deadline and indicate interest will be considered for available scholarships.

Scholarship Application Deadline

For the 2027–2029 intake, applicants seeking financial aid must submit by:

1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

This deadline also serves as an early application deadline for candidates who are self-funded.

Candidates seeking the Erasmus Mundus scholarship should treat this as the critical application deadline.

When Will Scholarship Results Be Released?

First-round admission decisions, including EMJM scholarship results, are scheduled to become available in the applicant portal on:

14 April 2027.

The deadline for appeals against first-round decisions is:

20 April 2027.

Self-Funded Deadline for Non-EU/EEA Residents

Candidates who:

  • Do not want to be considered for financial aid, and
  • Are residents outside the EU/EEA

have a later deadline:

15 April 2027 at 23:59 CET.

Their admission decisions are expected by:

30 June 2027

with appeals due by:

6 July 2027.

Self-Funded Deadline for EU/EEA Residents

EU/EEA residents who do not require financial aid may apply until:

1 July 2027 at 23:59 CET.

Their decisions are expected on:

15 July 2027

with appeals due by:

21 July 2027.

Official Academic Records Deadline

The deadline for successful applicants to submit official academic records is:

31 July 2027.

Candidates should make arrangements early if their universities require significant processing time to produce official documentation.

Complete 2027–2029 Admissions Timeline

The major dates are:

  • 1 September 2026: Applications expected to open
  • 1 December 2026, 23:59 CET: Financial-aid and early self-funded deadline
  • 14 April 2027: First-round decisions, including EMJM scholarships
  • 15 April 2027, 23:59 CET: Self-funded deadline for non-EU/EEA residents
  • 20 April 2027: First-round appeal deadline
  • 30 June 2027: Decisions for self-funded non-EU/EEA applicants
  • 1 July 2027, 23:59 CET: Self-funded deadline for EU/EEA residents
  • 6 July 2027: Non-EU/EEA self-funded appeal deadline
  • 15 July 2027: EU/EEA self-funded decisions
  • 21 July 2027: EU/EEA self-funded appeal deadline
  • 31 July 2027: Official academic-record deadline

The financial-aid deadline of 1 December 2026 is the most important date for anyone hoping to receive the Erasmus Mundus scholarship.

Appeals

Applications meeting the formal eligibility requirements are reviewed by at least two evaluators.

Applicants may appeal admission decisions, but the appeals procedure is limited.

Simply repeating information already included in the original application is not considered sufficient grounds for appeal.

Decisions are overturned only on:

Procedural grounds.

Candidates therefore need to ensure that the original application is as strong and complete as possible.

Deferral Policy

Mundus MAPP generally does not offer deferrals to applicants unable to arrive at the beginning of the first term because of:

  • Visa problems
  • Financial difficulties

The Consortium reserves the right to consider particularly well-justified requests exceptionally and on a case-by-case basis.

Applicants from visa-sensitive countries are strongly encouraged to apply by the earliest deadline.

How to Apply

Admissions are administered centrally by:

Central European University Private University

Candidates cannot submit separate Mundus MAPP applications directly to ISS, IBEI, or York.

Applicants must use the central CEU application system.

Only applications submitted through the designated CEU process will be considered.

Applicants need to:

  1. Select one mobility track.
  2. Complete the online application form.
  3. Upload all required documentation.
  4. Submit proof of English proficiency or applicable waiver documentation.
  5. Indicate whether they want financial-aid consideration.
  6. Submit before the relevant deadline.

Candidates do not need to pay the CEU application fee when applying only to Mundus MAPP. The fee applies if they also apply to other CEU programmes.

Official programme website:
https://www.mundusmapp.org/

Admissions information:
https://www.mundusmapp.org/admissions/

Admissions calendar:
https://www.mundusmapp.org/admissions-calendar/

Financial aid:
https://www.mundusmapp.org/financial-aid/

Required Supporting Documents

The user-provided programme information indicates that applicants must upload supporting documentation through the online application process.

Because the complete admissions checklist is maintained separately by Mundus MAPP and CEU, applicants should consult the current official checklist before submitting.

This is particularly important for:

  • Degree documents
  • Academic transcripts
  • English-language documentation
  • Statement of purpose
  • Residence evidence
  • Other formal admission materials

Applicants should avoid relying on older application checklists because requirements can change between admission cycles.

Practical Component of Mundus MAPP

Mundus MAPP is not designed solely around theoretical classroom study.

The programme includes a strong practical component through:

  • Internship
  • Study trip
  • Spring course
  • Case studies
  • Interaction with practitioners
  • Policy research

These activities allow students to observe policymaking processes directly and apply academic concepts to practical issues.

Internship Experience

Internships are part of the wider Mundus MAPP learning model.

They can help students:

  • Apply policy theories to real organizations
  • Gain professional experience
  • Build networks
  • Understand institutional processes
  • Explore potential career pathways
  • Collect empirical material relevant to research

The internship component also distinguishes Mundus MAPP from more purely academic public-policy master’s programmes.

Learning Outcomes

Graduates are expected to develop advanced knowledge across several areas.

Policy Theory and Institutions

Students develop systematic understanding of:

  • Public-policy theories
  • Policy paradigms
  • Policy concepts
  • Policy formation
  • Government institutions
  • International institutions
  • Intergovernmental coordination

Global and European Policy

Students learn about:

  • National policy processes
  • International policy
  • Transnational policymaking
  • European governance
  • Global governance
  • International development

Political, Economic and Legal Context

Graduates should be able to understand the:

  • Political
  • Economic
  • Legal
  • Geopolitical
  • Social

implications of public-policy formulation.

Policy Analysis and Problem Solving

Students learn how to:

  • Critically analyze policy problems
  • Evaluate public policies
  • Evaluate policy instruments
  • Use quantitative methods
  • Use qualitative methods
  • Develop research questions
  • Collect and analyze data
  • Produce policy reports
  • Advise decision-makers
  • Participate in policy design and implementation

These skills can be relevant across international organizations, governments, consulting, NGOs, and research institutions.

Interdisciplinary and Multicultural Skills

Mundus MAPP also emphasizes the ability to:

  • Work across social-science disciplines
  • Handle complex policy questions
  • Analyze incomplete information
  • Work in multicultural teams
  • Engage with different governance traditions
  • Understand accountability and transparency
  • Recognize ethical responsibilities in public service

The physical mobility component reinforces these skills by placing students within different institutional and national environments.

Communication Skills

Graduates are expected to develop professional-level English-language communication abilities.

They should be able to:

  • Produce academic and policy writing
  • Make presentations
  • Explain complex issues to specialist audiences
  • Communicate with non-specialists
  • Present evidence and recommendations clearly

These competencies are valuable for policy careers requiring frequent interaction among government officials, researchers, donors, civil society, and international partners.

Career Relevance

Mundus MAPP is explicitly designed to prepare future academic and policy leaders.

Graduates may pursue careers across areas such as:

  • International organizations
  • Government ministries
  • European institutions
  • NGOs
  • Development agencies
  • Policy consulting
  • Think tanks
  • Research institutions
  • International development
  • Public administration
  • Academia
  • Private-sector public policy

Different mobility tracks allow students to align their education with different professional priorities.

Tips for Preparing a Competitive Mundus MAPP Application

1. Choose Your Mobility Track Carefully

Applicants can apply to only one track.

Do not select a track simply because one partner university is more familiar to you.

Consider whether your interests align more strongly with:

  • Global Public Policy
  • European Public Policy
  • Political Economy and Development
  • Governance and Development

Your choice should reinforce your academic and career objectives.

2. Prioritize the December 1 Deadline if You Need Funding

Scholarships are limited and competitive.

If you want to be considered for either major financial-aid opportunities, submit by:

1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET.

Do not confuse this with the later deadlines for self-funded candidates.

3. Make the Motivation Statement Personal

Mundus MAPP explicitly values authenticity.

Explain the experiences and policy questions that genuinely shaped your interest in the programme.

Avoid vague statements such as:

“I have always been passionate about public policy.”

Instead, demonstrate how specific academic, professional, volunteer, or lived experiences led to your policy interests.

4. Explain Why Your Chosen Track Fits You

A particularly strong statement should show why your chosen institutional combination is strategically relevant to your goals.

5. Highlight Relevant Work Experience

Professional experience is not mandatory, but relevant experience is considered positively.

Applicants can highlight:

  • Internships
  • Research
  • Government work
  • NGO experience
  • International organizations
  • Policy projects
  • Volunteering
  • Advocacy
  • Student leadership

where genuinely relevant.

6. Prepare English Tests Early

Late scores are not accepted.

Applicants requiring IELTS, TOEFL, PTE, Duolingo, or Cambridge testing should book their exam well before December.

7. Check the Mobility Rule Before Applying

Your current residence can affect which mobility track you are eligible to choose.

This requirement is unusual and should not be overlooked.

8. Be Realistic About Scholarship Competition

Only a limited number of EMJM scholarships are available, and they go to the highest-ranked candidates. The programme explicitly encourages applicants to investigate external funding as well.

Important Details at a Glance

Programme: Erasmus Mundus Master’s Program in Public Policy

Common name: Mundus MAPP

Intake: 2027–2029

Application opening: Expected 1 September 2026

Duration: Two years

Study mode: Full-time and in person

Degree: Joint Master of Arts in Public Policy

Scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarship

Scholarship value: €1,400 per month for 24 months

Maximum scholarship: €33,600

Tuition: Full tuition waiver for EMJM scholarship recipients

Institutional scholarship: 50% tuition waiver, no stipend

Financial-aid deadline: 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET

Non-EU/EEA self-funded deadline: 15 April 2027

EU/EEA self-funded deadline: 1 July 2027

Minimum GPA: 3.17/4.0 or equivalent

Degree requirement: Minimum three-year Bachelor’s degree

Preferred background: Social sciences or equivalent

Working/study language: English

Work experience: Not mandatory, but relevant experience is preferred

Conclusion

The Mundus MAPP Erasmus Mundus Master’s Program in Public Policy 2027–2029 offers an exceptional opportunity for students seeking a genuinely international graduate education in public policy.

Through its consortium of Central European University, the International Institute of Social Studies, IBEI, and the University of York, the programme allows students to study in two different European countries while specializing in one of four areas: Global Public Policy, European Public Policy, Political Economy and Development, or Governance and Development.

The programme combines rigorous academic training with internships, study trips, research, practical policy analysis, and engagement with practitioners.

Outstanding applicants from both inside and outside the European Union can compete for Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarships worth up to €33,600 over 24 months, together with a full tuition-fee waiver. A separate Institutional Scholarship offering a 50% tuition waiver is also available for each study track.

Applicants normally need a recognized three-year Bachelor’s degree, at least Upper Second/2.1 where applicable, a minimum GPA of 3.17/4.0 or equivalent, appropriate academic preparation, and sufficient English proficiency.

Mundus MAPP is open internationally, but all students must comply with its compulsory physical mobility requirement.

Applications for the 2027–2029 cohort are expected to open on 1 September 2026. Candidates seeking financial aid should pay particular attention to the 1 December 2026 at 23:59 CET scholarship deadline.

Applicants should begin preparing early, particularly if they need an English-language test, university documents, mobility evidence, or time to develop a strong and personal statement of purpose.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Nature Restoration Academy 2026, a free training initiative designed to develop practical skills in marine and freshwater ecosystem restoration.

Organized and hosted by the SUBMARINER Network for Blue Growth, the programme combines an online introductory session with an intensive two-day, in-person training event at the organization’s office in Berlin, Germany. Selected participants will learn through expert lectures, practical workshops, European restoration case studies, digital monitoring approaches, and a multi-stakeholder negotiation simulation.

The programme is intended to help the next generation of restoration professionals translate environmental research and scientific knowledge into practical action. It will address the recovery of rivers, lakes, wetlands, coastal ecosystems, seas, and connected aquatic environments across the land–freshwater–marine continuum.

Participation is free, but only 30 places are available. Applicants must submit their applications by September 15, 2026. Selected participants will be notified by October 1, 2026.

Full details are available in the official SUBMARINER Network announcement.

Nature Restoration Academy 2026: Key Information

Programme information Details
Programme name Nature Restoration Academy
Main subject Marine and freshwater ecosystem restoration
Host organization SUBMARINER Network for Blue Growth
Funding organization EIT Water
Supporting organization Poul Due Jensen Foundation, also known as the Grundfos Foundation
Online baseline session October 6, 2026
In-person training dates October 29–30, 2026
Location SUBMARINER Network office, Berlin, Germany
Duration One online session followed by two days of in-person training
Participation fee Free of charge
Available places Maximum of 30 participants
Travel assistance A contribution may be available for participants travelling from outside Germany
Application deadline September 15, 2026
Selection notification By October 1, 2026
Application requirement Motivation statement and short CV
Application form Nature Restoration Academy Application Form

What Is the Nature Restoration Academy?

The Nature Restoration Academy is a new capacity-building initiative focused on practical methods for restoring marine and freshwater ecosystems.

The programme responds to the growing need for people who can connect environmental science, public policy, community participation, monitoring systems, and sustainable finance with real restoration projects. Its purpose is not limited to explaining restoration concepts theoretically. Instead, the Academy aims to develop practical understanding that participants can apply in their studies, employment, research, policy work, conservation programmes, or community initiatives.

The Academy covers ecosystems as an interconnected continuum. This means restoration is not treated as a series of isolated activities. Rivers, lakes, wetlands, estuaries, coasts, and marine environments are considered connected systems in which changes in one area may affect conditions elsewhere.

For example, freshwater quality can influence coastal ecosystems, while wetland degradation may affect biodiversity, water storage, flood management, nutrient flows, and surrounding communities. An integrated restoration approach therefore requires coordination across scientific disciplines, geographic boundaries, institutions, and stakeholder groups.

The programme has been designed to help participants understand these relationships and convert restoration knowledge into implementable solutions.

Who Organizes the Nature Restoration Academy?

The Academy is organized and hosted by the SUBMARINER Network for Blue Growth.

The SUBMARINER Network is a cooperation platform that connects research and educational institutions, public authorities, civil society organizations, business support institutions, and private companies working within the sustainable blue economy.

Although the network is rooted in the Baltic Sea Region, its partnerships and activities extend across Europe and beyond. Its work includes marine conservation, protected areas, sustainable aquaculture, blue biotechnology, maritime spatial planning, ecosystem restoration, policy development, innovation, and capacity-building.

The Nature Restoration Academy is funded by EIT Water and supported by the Poul Due Jensen Foundation, also known as the Grundfos Foundation.

Why Marine and Freshwater Restoration Training Matters

Aquatic ecosystems provide essential environmental, social, and economic services. Healthy rivers, lakes, wetlands, coastal areas, and seas can support biodiversity, water quality, climate resilience, sustainable livelihoods, food systems, recreation, tourism, and community well-being.

However, restoration projects are often technically and institutionally complex. Successful implementation may require cooperation among:

  • Scientists and researchers
  • Environmental authorities
  • Local governments
  • Conservation organizations
  • Businesses and investors
  • Marine and freshwater practitioners
  • Community groups
  • Citizen scientists
  • Energy developers
  • Landowners
  • Fisheries and aquaculture stakeholders
  • Civil society organizations
  • Funding institutions

Restoration professionals must understand ecological processes, but they may also need skills in stakeholder engagement, monitoring, project design, policy implementation, business planning, and funding.

The Nature Restoration Academy has been structured around this practical reality. Its combination of scientific content, case studies, workshops, simulations, and financing discussions is intended to help participants understand how restoration projects move from ideas and policies to implementation.

Structure of the Nature Restoration Academy

The programme consists of three connected components.

1. Online Baseline Session

Selected participants must first attend an online baseline session on October 6, 2026.

The session will provide a common foundation before the in-person event. It will draw on relevant material from the Blue Bio Techpreneurs course, Integrated Ocean Planning: Marine Protected Areas, Multi-Use and Business Pathways.

This common starting point should enable participants from different educational and professional backgrounds to take part more effectively in the advanced discussions and workshops held in Berlin.

The application form specifically asks candidates to confirm whether they can attend the October 6 online session. Selected applicants are expected to participate in both the online and in-person components.

2. Two-Day Training Event in Berlin

The main in-person programme will take place at the SUBMARINER Network’s Berlin office on October 29 and 30, 2026.

The two-day event will combine:

  • Lectures delivered by programme partners and invited experts
  • Marine and freshwater restoration case studies
  • Practical and interactive workshops
  • Discussions on nature-based restoration approaches
  • A multi-stakeholder negotiation simulation
  • Digital monitoring and citizen-science content
  • Sessions on project funding and business models
  • A dedicated discussion on gender equality within the sector

The limited cohort of 30 participants is likely to support active engagement, group work, peer learning, and direct interaction with trainers and other participants.

3. New Online Restoration Module

Sessions delivered during the Berlin event will be recorded and used to develop a new online restoration module.

The module will be added to the Blue Bio Techpreneurs course hosted on FutureLearn. This will allow the lessons, case studies, and expertise shared in Berlin to reach a much larger international audience after the in-person event.

When announcing the Academy, SUBMARINER reported that the existing course had already reached 464 learners from more than 80 countries. The linked FutureLearn course provides theoretical foundations in marine protected areas, maritime spatial planning, ocean multi-use, conservation governance, business planning, and sustainable blue-economy development.

The Nature Restoration Academy adds a more practical, in-person restoration component to this existing learning framework.

Main Training Topics

The programme will cover a broad selection of issues affecting the planning, implementation, monitoring, and financial sustainability of restoration projects.

Nature-Based Solutions

Participants will examine how nature-based solutions can be used to restore marine and freshwater ecosystems.

Nature-based solutions generally work with natural ecological processes to address environmental and social challenges. Within aquatic restoration, these approaches may involve rebuilding ecosystem functions, improving habitat quality, strengthening biodiversity, or increasing resilience to environmental pressures.

The Academy will connect these concepts with practical marine and freshwater restoration work.

European Restoration Case Studies

Real restoration case studies from Europe will be used to demonstrate how projects are designed and implemented in practice.

Case-based learning can help participants understand:

  • How restoration priorities are selected
  • Which stakeholders need to be involved
  • How ecological objectives are translated into activities
  • What implementation challenges may arise
  • How project results can be monitored
  • Which lessons can be transferred to other locations

These examples should allow participants to compare restoration strategies across different ecosystems and institutional settings.

Citizen Science

The programme will explore the role of citizen science in restoration.

Citizen science can involve members of the public in observing environmental changes, collecting ecological data, reporting species, monitoring water conditions, or supporting long-term project evaluation.

When properly designed, citizen-science programmes can expand monitoring capacity while improving public understanding and local ownership of restoration initiatives.

Digital Monitoring

Participants will also examine digital approaches to monitoring marine and freshwater restoration.

Digital monitoring can help project teams collect, organize, analyse, and communicate environmental information more effectively. Depending on the project, this may include remote sensing, digital mapping, mobile data collection, automated sensors, databases, or online reporting systems.

The Academy will consider how these tools can contribute to evidence-based restoration planning and evaluation.

Restoration in Offshore Wind Parks

One specialized topic will address restoration within offshore wind parks.

The rapid development of offshore renewable energy creates both challenges and potential opportunities for marine ecosystems. Restoration and nature-inclusive planning must therefore consider the relationship between energy infrastructure, marine habitats, biodiversity, fishing activity, protected areas, and other uses of ocean space.

This session should be particularly relevant to professionals interested in offshore renewable energy, marine spatial planning, environmental assessment, nature-inclusive design, and biodiversity protection.

Business Models for Restoration

The Academy will examine the business models that can support restoration activities over time.

A restoration project may have a strong ecological justification but still struggle if it lacks a sustainable operational and financial structure. Participants will therefore consider how restoration initiatives can connect environmental objectives with viable delivery models.

Relevant questions may include:

  • Who finances the initial project?
  • Who is responsible for long-term management?
  • Which organizations benefit from restoration?
  • Can ecosystem services be incorporated into the project model?
  • How can public, private, philanthropic, and community resources be combined?
  • How can restoration activities continue after short-term project funding ends?

Funding Mechanisms

Closely related to business-model development, the Academy will explore financing mechanisms for marine and freshwater restoration.

This component is important because restoration projects may rely on multiple funding sources. These can include public programmes, environmental funds, foundations, private investment, corporate partnerships, research funding, community finance, or blended-finance arrangements.

The training is expected to help participants understand that securing initial funding is only one part of project development. Long-term maintenance, monitoring, governance, and institutional ownership must also be considered.

MPA Game: Multi-Stakeholder Negotiation Simulation

The Berlin programme will include the MPA Game, an interactive simulation involving multi-stakeholder negotiation.

MPA refers to a Marine Protected Area. Decisions concerning these areas may involve conservation authorities, local communities, researchers, fishing interests, tourism operators, energy developers, businesses, and other stakeholders.

The simulation will allow participants to experience the challenges of balancing environmental protection with social and economic interests. It is designed to build skills in:

  • Stakeholder analysis
  • Negotiation
  • Conflict management
  • Collaborative decision-making
  • Policy interpretation
  • Communication
  • Compromise and consensus-building

Gender Equality in Marine and Freshwater Sectors

The programme will include a dedicated gender-equality session delivered by WIN-BIG.

This session will examine the importance of equal participation and opportunity within marine, freshwater, conservation, and blue-economy sectors. It will help participants consider how gender perspectives can be incorporated into environmental initiatives, professional development, decision-making, and sectoral leadership.

Benefits of Participating

Selected participants can expect several potential benefits from the programme:

  • Free participation in a specialized restoration academy
  • Practical training in marine and freshwater restoration
  • Exposure to European restoration case studies
  • Interaction with experts and practitioners
  • Participation in workshops and negotiation simulations
  • Knowledge of citizen-science and digital-monitoring approaches
  • Better understanding of restoration business models
  • Exposure to restoration funding mechanisms
  • Learning related to offshore wind and nature-inclusive development
  • A stronger understanding of stakeholder engagement
  • Opportunities to connect with other early-career professionals, students, and practitioners
  • Participation in discussions concerning gender equality in the sector
  • A possible contribution toward travel expenses for participants travelling from outside Germany

The programme announcement does not promise employment, a research grant, a stipend, or a fully funded trip. Its principal benefit is free access to the training programme and a possible contribution toward eligible travel costs.

Participation Cost and Travel Support

Participation in the Nature Restoration Academy is free of charge. Selected applicants will not be required to pay a programme registration or tuition fee.

The organizers also state that a contribution toward travel costs is available for participants coming from outside Germany.

Applicants should understand the wording carefully. A travel contribution is not necessarily the same as complete reimbursement. The announcement does not specify:

  • The maximum travel contribution
  • Whether all selected international participants will receive it
  • Whether accommodation is covered
  • Whether meals are covered
  • Whether visa expenses are covered
  • When travel funds will be paid
  • Which transport methods are eligible
  • Whether participants must pay first and claim reimbursement later

The application form asks candidates to state:

  • Where they will travel from
  • The approximate distance to Berlin
  • Their estimated travel cost

Applicants who require financial assistance should provide an accurate and reasonable travel estimate. They should also request clarification from the organizers before making non-refundable travel arrangements.

Who Should Consider Applying?

The Academy is intended for people who are already engaged in, studying, or beginning a career connected to marine or freshwater restoration.

Suitable backgrounds may include:

  • Environmental science
  • Marine biology
  • Freshwater ecology
  • Aquatic ecosystem management
  • Conservation
  • Biodiversity
  • Marine protected areas
  • Wetland restoration
  • River or lake restoration
  • Coastal management
  • Environmental policy
  • Marine spatial planning
  • Citizen science
  • Environmental monitoring
  • Sustainable blue economy
  • Offshore renewable energy
  • Nature-based solutions
  • Environmental project management
  • Restoration finance
  • Sustainability

The organizers have not published a specific age limit, minimum degree requirement, mandatory number of years of experience, or required professional title.

However, applicants should be able to demonstrate a credible connection to marine or freshwater restoration through their studies, work, research, projects, volunteering, or professional interests.

Application Requirements

Applicants must complete the official online form and provide the requested information.

The form includes the following sections:

Personal and Professional Information

Applicants must provide:

  • Full name
  • Email address
  • Organization or university
  • Department or subject of study
  • Professional sector
  • Country of residence
  • Nationality
  • Gender
  • Current role or professional profile

The application form states that nationality and gender information will be used only for anonymized, aggregated reporting to EIT Water and will not be published with the applicant’s name.

Motivation Statement

Applicants must submit a short motivation statement. The online form provides a field with a 1,000-character limit.

The statement should explain:

  • Why the applicant wants to attend the Academy
  • How their background relates to marine or freshwater restoration
  • What they expect to learn
  • How they will use the training
  • What experience or perspective they can contribute
  • Why they are a suitable candidate for one of the 30 places

Because the available space is limited, applicants should avoid general statements and provide specific evidence of their interest or involvement.

Short Curriculum Vitae

Applicants must upload a short CV.

The CV should prioritize information relevant to restoration, environmental science, conservation, policy, monitoring, sustainability, the blue economy, or related subjects.

Relevant content may include:

  • Education
  • Current position or academic programme
  • Environmental or restoration experience
  • Research projects
  • Relevant employment
  • Internships
  • Volunteer activities
  • Publications
  • Technical skills
  • Community projects
  • Professional memberships
  • Training and certifications

Attendance Confirmation

Applicants must confirm whether they can attend the online baseline session on October 6, 2026.

Selected participants are expected to attend both the online baseline session and the two-day event in Berlin. Candidates who cannot participate in both components may be less suitable for selection.

Travel Information

Applicants must identify:

  • Their point of departure
  • The approximate distance to Berlin
  • The estimated cost of travelling to Berlin

This information may help the organizers assess travel-support requirements for participants coming from outside Germany.

Dietary and Accessibility Information

The form allows applicants to disclose dietary requirements, including vegan, vegetarian, and gluten-free options.

Applicants may also provide details of any accessibility requirements relevant to their participation.

Data, Newsletter, and Media Information

The application includes fields concerning:

  • SUBMARINER Network newsletter updates
  • Processing of personal data for event administration and anonymized reporting
  • Photography and filming during the event

The event will be photographed and filmed for promotional and educational purposes by EIT Water, the Poul Due Jensen Foundation, and the SUBMARINER Network. Recorded sessions will also contribute to the future online restoration module.

Applicants should read the consent language and the SUBMARINER Network privacy policy carefully before submitting the form.

How to Apply

Applicants should complete the following steps:

  1. Review the official programme announcement.
  2. Confirm availability for the online session on October 6, 2026.
  3. Confirm availability to travel to Berlin for October 29–30, 2026.
  4. Prepare a concise motivation statement within the application field’s 1,000-character limit.
  5. Prepare a short, relevant CV.
  6. Estimate the travel distance and cost to Berlin.
  7. Complete all personal, academic, professional, dietary, accessibility, and consent sections.
  8. Review the information carefully.
  9. Submit the form before September 15, 2026.

Applications must be submitted through the official Nature Restoration Academy application form.

Important Dates

Stage Date
Application deadline September 15, 2026
Selection notification By October 1, 2026
Online baseline session October 6, 2026
In-person Berlin training October 29–30, 2026

The official announcement does not specify a deadline time or time zone. Applicants should therefore submit before the final date rather than waiting until the last few hours.

Separate Opportunity for Lecturers and Workshop Leaders

In addition to participant applications, the SUBMARINER Network is inviting restoration experts to contribute a lecture or case study to the Berlin programme.

Potential contributors should:

  • Have expertise in marine or freshwater restoration
  • Be able to participate in person in Berlin
  • Be prepared to deliver a session of approximately one hour
  • Consider combining a short lecture with an interactive workshop
  • Be willing for the session to be recorded and incorporated into the new FutureLearn restoration module

Experts interested in contributing should contact the organizers at info@submariner-network.eu.

This contributor invitation is separate from the standard application process for the 30 participant places.

Tips for a Strong Application

Because only 30 participants will be selected, applicants should make their relevance clear.

A strong application should:

  • Establish a direct connection with marine or freshwater restoration.
  • Mention a specific academic, professional, research, or community project.
  • Explain which Academy topics are most relevant to the applicant.
  • Describe how the knowledge will be applied after the programme.
  • Show an interest in practical implementation, not only theory.
  • Demonstrate willingness to participate actively in workshops and simulations.
  • Confirm availability for both programme components.
  • Provide a concise and relevant CV.
  • Give an accurate estimate of travel costs.
  • Submit before the deadline.

Applicants should not describe the programme as fully funded. Participation is free, and a travel contribution may be available for people travelling from outside Germany, but complete coverage of travel, accommodation, meals, visas, or other costs has not been announced.

Conclusion

The Nature Restoration Academy 2026 provides a valuable opportunity to develop practical skills in marine and freshwater ecosystem restoration through a combination of online learning, expert instruction, applied case studies, interactive workshops, and stakeholder simulation.

The programme’s focus on nature-based solutions, citizen science, digital monitoring, offshore wind parks, restoration finance, business models, negotiation, and gender equality reflects the wide range of capabilities required to deliver successful environmental restoration projects.

Participation is free, and a contribution toward travel expenses may be available for selected participants travelling from outside Germany. However, places are highly limited, with only 30 participants expected to join the programme.

Eligible candidates should prepare a focused motivation statement and short CV, confirm that they can attend the October 6 online session and the October 29–30 Berlin event, and submit the official application by September 15, 2026.
